items.title: British Pound futures rebound as U.K. economic data beats expectations.
items.excerpt: British Pound futures tested their 200-day moving average before rebounding into positive territory, putting the contract on pace to snap a two-week streak of lower closes. The move was supported by stronger-than-expected U.K. economic data, with July GDP rising 0.4% and year-over-year growth hitting 1.6%. The robust data adds complexity to next Thursday's Bank of England meeting, where markets widely expect rates to remain at 3.75% amid pushback from Governor Andrew Bailey on the necessity of near-term hikes.

items.title: Treasury yields jump 24 bps as the Fed weighs a rate hike.
items.excerpt: Treasury yields are in focus for the week ahead after the 2-Year yield jumped 24 bps and the 5-Year yield rose 21 bps, marking the largest weekly increase since April 2025. The moves set the stage for a critical week of global central bank action. The FOMC announces its rate decision on Wednesday, accompanied by an updated Summary of Economic Projections. The probability of a 25 bps hike hit 86.5% following recent CPI data. Decisions from the Bank of England and the Bank of Japan follow on Thursday. The economic calendar also features U.S. Retail Sales, global CPI data, and regional manufacturing indicators, while the earnings slate remains light with five major companies reporting.

items.title: Oracle vs Adobe: AI is rewarding scarcity and punishing uncertainty
items.excerpt: Key takeaways Oracle is turning artificial intelligence demand into real cloud revenue, but the bill for building capacity remains enormous. Adobe s artificial intelligence products are growing quickly, yet investors still want proof that adoption protects pricing power. The bigger lesson is simple: artificial intelligence creates value only when it improves economics or strengthens competitive advantages. Oracle and Adobe reported earnings on 10 September 2026, but they offered investors two very different artificial intelligence stories. Oracle, once mainly known for databases, is spending heavily to become a major supplier of computing power. Ahead of the ECB meeting, crude oil prices were already surging higher and sending the US dollar higher as well amidst cratering risk sentiment. And then the ECB delivered a hawkish surprise on top of its expected 25-bp rate hike that sent yields ripping higher the world over. The German 2-year yield surged a stunning 16 basis points after the ECB meeting on the one-two of the ECB s raised headline and core CPI forecasts for next year and 2028 and the multi-dollar rise in crude oil prices. items.title: Euro FX futures hold range-bound as ECB hikes rates 25 bps.
items.excerpt: Todd Colvin unpacks the latest price action in Euro FX futures, which had a choppy session and settled near 1.1612 following the ECB's decision to hike rates by 25 basis points. With no clear guidance from President Lagarde on future moves, the market remains range-bound between 1.1550 and 1.1650. Colvin also highlights the CME Group Volatility Index (CVOL), noting that implied volatility remains firm across asset classes amid ongoing geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. Looking ahead, focus shifts to the U.S. Consumer Price Index and its potential impact on next week's Federal Reserve meeting.

Iaccino also covers the European Central Bank's decision to raise its deposit rate by 25 basis points and its impact on the euro. Finally, he previews the economic calendar, highlighting a $22 billion 30-Year Treasury bond auction, the ongoing corporate earnings slate, and upcoming gross domestic product and inflation data.

items.title: Japanese Yen futures rally ahead of Bank of Japan rate decision.
items.excerpt: Japanese Yen futures saw upward momentum, rallying in four of the last five sessions to climb 4.45% above the September low. The price action comes as the market anticipates a potential 25 bps rate increase at the upcoming Sept. 18 Bank of Japan meeting. Ongoing policy coordination between Tokyo and the U.S. Treasury, underscored by the July 31 yen intervention funded via euro reserves, continues to influence the currency's trajectory. Despite a softer second-quarter GDP revision, broader market expectations suggest economic conditions pose no immediate obstacle to further rate adjustments.

Bob also previews the upcoming ECB rate decision, where markets anticipate a 25 bps rate hike following a recent jump in inflation, and outlines the heavy slate of earnings, auctions, and economic data ahead.

items.title: Gold rangebound as weaker dollar offsets rate-hike and inflation risks
items.excerpt: Gold traders - and the algorithmic programmes that account for a significant share of day-to-day activity - are currently struggling to determine which of several competing themes will ultimately set the tone, overall keeping prices rangebound around USD 4,400. As the charts below illustrate, the clearest headwind has come from rising rate-hike expectations and higher bond yields, increasing the opportunity cost of holding a non-yielding asset such as gold. Against this backdrop, a softer dollar has provided support, while underlying investment demand through ETFs and futures has so far remained relatively resilient. Geopolitical uncertainty also remains elevated, with the latest flare-up in the Middle East helping to sustain gold s appeal as a portfolio diversifier and limiting downside…

items.title: Euro futures hold at 1.1625 ahead of ECB meeting.
items.excerpt: Todd Colvin of Mark IV Brokerage breaks down Euro futures as the currency holds near 1.1625 ahead of this week's European Central Bank meeting. Markets are currently pricing in a 25 basis point rate hike from the ECB, but attention remains focused on guidance regarding future policy if inflation remains elevated. Colvin highlights that despite upcoming risk events—including the ECB decision and U.S. CPI data—the CVOL index shows volatility dropping to three-week lows. Additionally, the latest Commitment of Traders data reveals speculators are covering net short positions, marking their smallest short exposure since mid-July.
